outline.chapter_title: Motivation and Historical Context of Recurrent Models
outline.description: Introduces the origins of recurrent neural networks, the vanishing gradient problem, and how the original LSTM solved it. Provides a timeline that leads to modern large‑scale language models and explains why revisiting LSTMs is worthwhile.
subtopics: The vanishing gradient problem in vanilla RNNs
Constant error carousel and gating in the original LSTM
Successes of LSTMs across domains (NLP, RL, scientific modeling)
Limitations of LSTMs that motivated the rise of Transformers
Key research question: scaling LSTMs to billions of parameters

outline.description: A complete, step‑by‑step derivation of the standard LSTM equations, its gating mechanisms, and the role of each parameter. Shows how the scalar cell state is updated and why each component is essential.
subtopics: Notation and basic forward‑pass equations
Input, forget, and output gates – sigmoid activation and bias terms
Cell input transformation and activation functions
Hidden‑state computation and output gating
Vector‑valued cells and recurrent weight matrices
Ablation insights: importance of each gate and connection

outline.chapter_title: Identified Limitations of the Standard LSTM
outline.description: Analyzes three fundamental shortcomings of the original architecture that hinder scaling and performance on language tasks.
subtopics: Inability to revise storage decisions (illustrated with Nearest‑Neighbor Search)
Limited scalar memory capacity and its effect on rare‑token prediction
Sequential hidden‑hidden connections → lack of parallelism
Empirical evidence from prior literature

outline.description: Introduces exponential activation for input/forget gates, explains why it resolves revision and capacity issues, and details the normalizer and stabilizer states that keep training numerically stable.
subtopics: Motivation for exponential gates
Mathematical form of exponential activation
Normaliser state nₜ and its role in scaling hidden output
Stabilizer state mₜ and log‑space re‑parameterization
Proof sketch that stabilized gates preserve gradients
Practical considerations (initialisation, overflow handling)

outline.chapter_title: sLSTM: Scalar Memory with Memory Mixing
outline.description: Defines the sLSTM variant, shows the full forward pass, explains how exponential gating and the normaliser are integrated, and describes the new memory‑mixing mechanism across cells and heads.
subtopics: sLSTM forward equations (cell, normaliser, hidden state)
Exponential vs. sigmoid forget gate options
Multiple memory cells and recurrent mixing matrices
Head‑wise processing and intra‑head mixing
Comparison to original multi‑cell LSTM
Implementation notes and CUDA acceleration

outline.chapter_title: mLSTM: Matrix Memory with Covariance Updates
outline.description: Presents the matrix‑memory extension, connects it to associative memory and fast‑weight programmers, and details the covariance update rule and its parallelisable formulation.
subtopics: From scalar cell to d×d memory matrix Cₜ
Key‑value formulation (kₜ, vₜ) and query‑based retrieval
Covariance (outer‑product) update rule and its optimality
Integration of exponential input/forget gates as learning/decay rates
Normaliser vector nₜ and safe division for hidden output
Parallel implementation and relationship to FlashAttention

outline.chapter_title: xLSTM Block Design: Residual Backbones and Up‑Projection
outline.description: Shows how sLSTM and mLSTM are wrapped inside modern residual blocks, explains the two up‑projection strategies (post‑ and pre‑projection), and connects to Cover’s theorem for high‑dimensional representation.
subtopics: Residual connection with pre‑LayerNorm
Post up‑projection block (used for sLSTM)
Pre up‑projection block (used for mLSTM)
Non‑linear summarisation of past information
Diagrammatic walk‑through of an xLSTM block
Compatibility with existing LLM backbones

outline.chapter_title: Full xLSTM Architecture and Model Scaling
outline.description: Describes how xLSTM blocks are stacked into deep models, discusses the mixture ratio notation xLSTM[a:b], and analyzes computational and memory complexity compared with Transformers and SSMs.
subtopics: Stacking strategy: number of blocks, depth vs. width
Mixing ratios of mLSTM and sLSTM blocks (e.g., xLSTM[7:1])
Linear time and constant memory with respect to sequence length
GPU memory footprint and throughput considerations
Comparison of parallel vs. sequential components

outline.chapter_title: Training Procedures for Large‑Scale xLSTM Models
outline.description: Covers practical aspects of training billion‑parameter xLSTMs: data preparation, mixed‑precision, optimizer settings, learning‑rate schedules, and tricks for stable exponential gating.
subtopics: Dataset used (SlimPajama) and tokenisation
Mixed‑precision training and gradient scaling
AdamW hyper‑parameters and warm‑up schedule
Initialising forget‑gate bias for long‑term retention
Batching, sequence length handling, and checkpointing
Integration with existing LLM training pipelines

outline.description: Explains the synthetic tasks used to isolate each new component (exponential gating, matrix memory) and presents the experimental setup and interpretation of results.
subtopics: Formal‑language/Parity and state‑tracking tasks
Nearest‑Neighbor Search as a revision test
Multi‑Query Associative Recall and memory capacity
Long Range Arena for context‑length robustness
Analysis of why Transformers/SSMs fail without mixing

outline.chapter_title: Empirical Evaluation on Real‑World Language Modeling
outline.description: Presents the full suite of language‑model experiments, from 15 B‑token to 300 B‑token training, covering validation perplexity, scaling laws, downstream evaluation, and long‑context extrapolation.
subtopics: Benchmarking protocol (validation perplexity, token budget)
Comparison table against GPT‑3, Llama, Mamba, RWKV, etc.
Ablation study: stepwise morphing from LSTM → xLSTM
Effect of exponential gating vs. matrix memory
Scaling curves and power‑law fits
Downstream task suite (common‑sense reasoning, PALOMA domains)
Length‑extrapolation results up to 16 k tokens

outline.chapter_title: Practical Considerations: Speed, Throughput, and Limitations
outline.description: Discusses inference speed, generation time, throughput versus batch size, and enumerates current limitations and open engineering challenges.
subtopics: Linear vs. quadratic scaling of generation time
Throughput measurements for xLSTM, Mamba, RWKV, Llama
CUDA kernel performance gaps and possible optimisations
Memory‑capacity vs. computational cost of d×d matrix
Initialisation sensitivities and maximum context length
Roadmap for future engineering improvements

outline.description: Reflects on the significance of scaling recurrent models, possible applications beyond NLP, and research avenues opened by xLSTM.
subtopics: Implications for reinforcement learning and scientific modeling
Potential hybrid architectures (Transformer‑RNN combos)
Exploring richer memory structures (tensor memories)
Investigating alternative normalisation/stabilisation tricks
Ethical considerations of large‑scale recurrent LLMs
